explain.say: Fog is simply a cloud touching the ground: billions of tiny water droplets hanging in the air. It forms when air near the ground cools until its water vapour condenses.

explain.say: Radiation fog forms on clear, calm nights. The ground loses heat to the open sky and cools the air just above it to its dew point, so by morning fog collects in valleys.

explain.say: Advection fog forms when warm, moist air drifts over a colder surface, such as a cold sea current or snowy ground. San Francisco's famous summer fog forms this way.

explain.say: When the Sun rises it warms the ground and the air, the droplets evaporate, and radiation fog lifts or burns off. Advection fog can linger as long as the cold surface and moist wind remain.

faq.a: Yes. Fog is a cloud that forms at ground level, made of tiny water droplets. If you walk through fog you are walking through a cloud.
asks: What is the difference between fog and a cloud?

faq.q: Why is fog common in valleys?
faq.a: On calm nights cold air is heavy and slides downhill, pooling in valleys. That air reaches its dew point first, so fog fills the valley while hilltops stay clear.
asks: Why does fog sit in low places?

faq.q: Why does fog disappear in the morning?
faq.a: Sunlight warms the ground and the air above it. Warmer air can hold more water vapour, so the droplets evaporate and the fog thins and lifts.

faq.q: What is the difference between fog and mist?
faq.a: They are the same thing in different amounts. Weather forecasters call it fog when you cannot see further than 1 kilometre, and mist when you can see further.
asks: Is mist the same as fog?

faq.q: Why is San Francisco so foggy?
faq.a: Cold water rises along the California coast. In summer, warm, moist ocean air passes over that cold water, cools to its dew point and rolls in as advection fog.

facts: Weather services call it fog when visibility is below 1 kilometre, and mist when it is 1 kilometre or more.
The Grand Banks off Newfoundland are among the foggiest places on Earth, where air warmed over the Gulf Stream drifts over the cold Labrador Current.

quiz.say: On a clear, calm night the ground cools and fog forms by morning. Which kind of fog is this?
quiz.show: Fog from the ground cooling on a clear night is…
quiz.why: Radiation fog forms when the ground loses heat to a clear sky and chills the air above it to its dew point.

wrong.1: Advection fog comes from moist air moving over a cold surface, not from the ground cooling overnight.
wrong.2: Sea smoke forms when very cold air moves over much warmer water.
